chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام about a man who pledges a slave, a garment, jewelry, or household goods, and the owner of the goods says to the mortgage-holder: 'You are permitted to wear this garment; wear the garment, benefit from the goods, and use the servant.'
He said: 'It is halal for him if he has made it halal for him, but I do not like that he should do it.'
I said: 'If he takes a house in pledge that has yield, to whom does the yield belong?' He said: 'To the owner of the house.'

I said: 'If he takes barren land in pledge, and the owner of the land says to him: Cultivate it for yourself?' He said: 'This is halal. This is not like that case. He cultivates it with his own wealth, so it is halal for him just as he has permitted it for him, because he cultivates it with his own wealth and develops it.'

key_terms.الْمُرْتَهِنِ: the pledge-holder or creditor holding collateral
key_terms.بِمَالِهِ: with his own wealth or financial resources
key_terms.حَلَالٌ: lawful and permitted in the legal sense
key_terms.غَلَّةٌ: yield, produce, or income generated from property
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: being granted lawful permission to use something
key_terms.يَرْهَنُ: to give something in pledge as collateral

ai.seo_question: Can a creditor benefit from property given as collateral in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith explains legal rulings related to pledged property and the creditor's benefit from it. It distinguishes between mere use of pledged items by permission, which is technically halal but disliked, and cultivation of barren pledged land with one's own resources, which is permitted because the benefit comes through the creditor's own investment. It also clarifies that the natural yield of a pledged house remains the right of its owner.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4117 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

"I asked Abu Ibrahim (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)) about a man who pledges a slave, garment, jewelry, or household items as collateral, and the owner of the property tells the creditor, 'You are permitted to use this garment, wear it, benefit from the property, and use the servant.'
The Imam (as) replied: 'It is lawful for him if the owner permits it, but I do not like him to do so.' "

I then asked: 'What if someone pledges a house that produces income, who does the income belong to?'
Imam (as) replied: 'The income belongs to the owner of the house.' "

I further asked: 'What if someone pledges a barren land and the owner of the land tells him to cultivate it for himself?'
Imam (as) replied: 'This is lawful. It is not the same as the previous case. He cultivates it with his own money, so it is lawful for him as the owner has permitted it, because he invests his own resources and develops the land.' "
